A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ConcreTizer study, with complete main text and appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI and Waymo restoration experiments, downstream object-detection evaluations, ablations and defense analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and 11 and the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain identical VOC and DCS components, training losses, intermediate-feature masking and voxel-center reconstruction. No algorithm or architecture changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use KITTI and Waymo for point-cloud restoration and downstream 3D object detection, with identical augmentation and noise scenarios.

E2.justification: Point Regression and UltraLiDAR retain the same participation in Tables 1, 2 and 11. The original-data reference and VOC comparison variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D specify identical splits, cropping, voxel sizes, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures. F1 thresholds remain 15 cm for KITTI and 30 cm for Waymo.

E4.justification: Component ablations, DCS instance and split-position analyses, voxelization analysis, augmentation/noise tests and qualitative examples are unchanged, including the appendix evidence.

E5.justification: The same averages and boxplots are retained. Neither the main text nor appendices change repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty reporting or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains deepest-layer ConcreTizer F1 scores of 0.9160 on KITTI and 0.9251 on Waymo.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and loss formulas in Section 4, Voxel Single-Point hypothesis in Appendix A and metric definitions in Appendix C are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, VOC/DCS contributions, restoration-effectiveness claims and conclusions about the vulnerability of 3D features.

C2.justification: Explanations of voxel dispersion, label imbalance and partitioning errors are identical. Section 6 and Appendix F retain the same parameter-access assumption, applicability boundaries and privacy–utility limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E and Tables 4–10 retain the same hardware, optimizer, hyperparameters, cropping instructions and architecture specifications. Resource references and licensing information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions and both reference lists match. The positioning relative to earlier inversion attacks, voxel-based feature extraction and LiDAR generation is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording, terminology and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page presentation changes through the added running conference header and updated first-page arXiv stamp. Figures 1–21, Tables 1–11, captions and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds publication-status information but preserves the scientific text, evidence, technical details and limitations throughout the main paper and appendices. The header and version-stamp updates do not materially change clarity, reproducibility or evidential strength.
